  - text: CLASS 8 · PRACTICAL GEOMETRY
  - heading "Triangle Construction by SSS ☆" [level=1]
  - paragraph: "Learning objective: Construct a unique triangle when all three side lengths are known."
  - text: ♙ Class 8 ▦ Practical Geometry ▦ Construction ◉ 24 min
  - link "← School lessons":

  - heading "Build your triangle (SSS Construction)" [level=2]
  - paragraph: 1) Set the three side lengths. 2) Use the points A and B to set the base. 3) Intersect the two arcs to place point C.
  - button "Reset":
    - img
    - text: Reset
  - button "Replay steps":
    - img
    - text: Replay steps
  - complementary:
    - heading "SIDE LENGTHS" [level=3]
    - text: AB (base) 7 cm
    - slider "AB (base) length": "7"
    - text: 3 15 AC 5 cm
    - slider "AC length": "5"
    - text: 3 15 BC 6 cm
    - slider "BC length": "6"
    - text: 3 15
    - complementary:
      - text: ✓ Triangle is valid
      - paragraph: 5 + 6 > 7, 7 + 6 > 5, 7 + 5 > 6
  - article:
    - list:
      - text: Construction steps
      - listitem:
        - text: 1 Draw AB = 7 cm
        - img
      - listitem:
        - text: 2 Arc from A, r = 5 cm
        - img
      - listitem:
        - text: 3 Arc from B, r = 6 cm
        - img
      - listitem: 4 Intersection = C
      - listitem: 5 Join A-C and B-C
    - img "SSS triangle and compass arc intersections":
      - slider "Intersection point C"
      - text: A B C 7 cm 5 cm 6 cm
    - text: ✓ Triangle constructed ♧ Drag point C along the intersection to explore.
    - button "Zoom out": −
    - text: 100%
    - button "Zoom in": ＋
  - complementary: "ⓘ Rule: A triangle exists only when the sum of any two sides is greater than the third."
  - article:
    - heading "Why it works" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Point C is at a distance AC from A and BC from B. The only location that satisfies both distances is at the intersection of the two arcs, so the triangle is unique.
    - img: C A B
    - text: 5 cm 6 cm 7 cm
  - article:
    - heading "Worked example" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Construct sides 5 cm, 6 cm, and 7 cm.
    - list:
      - listitem: Set AB = 7 cm.
      - listitem: Draw an arc from A with radius 5 cm.
      - listitem: Draw an arc from B with radius 6 cm.
      - listitem: Mark their intersection as C.
      - listitem: Join AC and BC.
    - complementary:
      - text: "✓ Result: △ABC with AB = 7 cm, AC = 5 cm, BC = 6 cm"
      - paragraph: Unique triangle constructed.
  - article:
    - heading "⚠ Common misconception" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Picking the arc intersection without preserving both radii changes the specified sides.
    - text: "Correct: C is on both arcs."
    - img: C
    - text: "Incorrect: C not on both arcs."
    - img: C
  - article:
    - heading "♢ Try it yourself" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "Challenge: Construct a △ABC with sides 4 cm, 5 cm, and 6 cm."
    - complementary:
      - heading "SIDE LENGTHS" [level=3]
      - text: AB (base) 6 cm
      - slider "AB (base) length": "6"
      - text: 3 15 AC 4 cm
      - slider "AC length": "4"
      - text: 3 15 BC 5 cm
      - slider "BC length": "5"
      - text: 3 15
      - button "Check construction"
    - img "SSS triangle and compass arc intersections":
      - slider "Intersection point C"
      - text: A B C 6 cm 4 cm 5 cm
    - text: ♧ Drag C to the intersection of the arcs.
  - complementary:
    - heading "What to do" [level=2]
    - paragraph: ✓ Set the three side lengths as given.
    - paragraph: ✓ Intersect the arcs to place C.
    - paragraph: ✓ Join AC and BC.
    - paragraph: ✓ Click ‘Check construction’.
    - heading "♧ Need a hint?" [level=2]
    - paragraph: When C is on both arcs, it will be a distance of 4 cm from A and 5 cm from B.
